NEW Y.M.C.A. PROJECT 
FOR 
EASTERN MONTREAL 
Plans for a bi-lingual Vocational Services and 
Information Center in eastern Montreal were announced 


today by Mr. Basil Burgess, Chairman of the Internation- 


al ¥.M.C.A. Board. 


The new Y.M.C.A. project, located in offices above 
the Boulevard Shopping Center, will open on June 10th. 
Initially its main function will be to provide informat- 
ion to youth and young adults about the various courses 
and programs available from all sources in Montreal to 
those wishing to prepare themselves for greater employ- 


ment opportunities. 


A recent Y.M.C.A. survey found that many younger 
workers and students are not fully aware of the wide 
range of services and programs available through public 
and private agencies in Montreal. Some young people need 
assistance in assessing their needs for further training 
and education and in locating appropriate services avail- 
able to them. Some need help in planning their approach 
to the whole question of employment and will welcome the 
opportunity to talk things over with an experienced and 


interested staff member. 


"All too often we underestimate the wide range of 
valuable programs and services currently available through 
government programs, school guidance departments, edu- 


cational, vocational, and technical institutions and 


a 
other concerned community organizations," said Mr.Bruce 
McFarlane, who will direct the new project. "The Y.M.C.A. 
hopes to work in active partnership with all groups and 
agencies now working in the whole field of manpower de- 
velopment. Montreal is most fortunate in terms of the 
extent of its resources and our job will be to serve as 
an information headcuarters for persons concerned about 


their present qualifications." 


Bruce McFarlane, a native of Montreal, was engaged 
in personnel work in Montreal's east end for several 
years prior to joining the staff of International Y.M.C.A. 
in 1960. He is bi-lingual and has gained some knowledge 
of several languages through his work in adult education 
at International Branch in recent years. For several 
months he has conducted a survey of the Eastern Comm- 
unities and is familiar with the work of the various 


agencies and groups now serving eastern Montreal. 


During June and July, the new Y.M.C.A. Center will 
welcome visits and inquiries from ail interested groups 
and persons about their concerns for further education 


and training and other employment questions. 


‘Based on our experience during the summer, the 
work of the new Center will be reviewed by an advisory 
committee representing business, education and related 
groups with a view towards establishing more definite 
targets for action during the fall and winter months. 


The Montreal Y.M.C.A. is vitally interested in the needs 


-3- 


of unemployed youth and in encouraging young people to 
work together in tackling their common problems and 
concerns," said Mr. McFarlane. In establishing the new 
program the Montreal Y.M.C.A. hopes to further strengthen 
its partnership with the various groups at work for the 


development of the total community. 


Anyone wishing further information about the 
Y.M.C.A. Vocational Service Center should contact Bruce 
McFarlane at the new office in the Boulevard Shopping 
Genter. Information is also available through the bus- 
iness office at International Y.M.C.A. which is open 


daily until 10 pm. 


Persons wishing further details should contact; 


R.B. McFarlane, 
26 Jean Talon St.East, Rm. 10. 
Phone 725- 305 


OR 
c/o International Branch YMCA. 


5550 Park Ave. 
Phone 271- 639

de 1'U.C.J.G. (Y¥.M.C.A.) annoncé aujourd'hui l'ouverture 
prochaine d'un centre d'information et d'orientation pvro- 
fessionnelle bilingue dans l'est de Montréal. 

Ce centre ouvrira ses portes le 10 juin a l'étage 
supérieur du Centre d'Achat Boulevard. Au début, son 
principal but sera de fournir des renseignments aux jeunes 
et aux jeunes adultes sur les divers cours et programmes 
offerts a Montréal & ceux qui désirent se préparer a de 
meilleurs emplois. 

Une enquéte récente de 1'U.C.J.G. a démontré que de 
nombreux jeunes travailleurs et étudiants ne sont pas tres 
au courant du vaste choix de services et de programmes mis 
a leur disposition par les organismes privés et publics a 
Montréal. Quelques jeunes ont besoin d'aide pour évaluer

leur conviennent. Dtautres ont besoin de conseils pour se

du personnel qui s'intéresse a eux.

ucation des adultes A la liliale internationale pendant
